newsitem.title: USA: White House says in early stages of Fed search.
newsitem.headline: White House says in early stages of Fed search.

text.p: The White House said on Friday that it was in the early stages of its search for replacements for two departing Federal Reserve Board members and said the new nominees were unlikely to be in place in time for the central bank's Feb. 4-5 policy-making meeting.

"We're very early in the process and it's hard to imagine, given where we are in the process, that we would have nominees in place in time for that meeting," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

Earlier on Friday the Federal Reserve said that Fed Governor Lawrence Lindsey had submitted his resignation, effective Feb. 5, adding that he would not attend the Feb. 4-5 meeting of the policy-making Federal Open Market Commitee.

Lindsey's departure follows that of Fed. Governor Janet Yellen, who has been appointed chairman of the White House Council of Economic Advisers (CEA). Yellen also will not attend the early February FOMC meeting.

McCurry told reporters Gene Sperling, the newly named chairman of the White House National Economic Council, has begun a process to canvas the academic, economic and financial communities for candidates.
Among the government agencies included in the process are the Treasury Department, the Office of Management and Budget and the CEA, McCurry said.
"They are casting a very wide net. We are very early in the process. We are not on the verge of any nominations," McCurry added."
McCurry said that Erskine Bowles, Clinton's chief of staff, would likely make formal reccomendations on the replacements to Clinton.
